chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said regarding a man who gave a man a promissory note (wariq) in exchange for a servant (wasif) for a specified term, so the owner said to him, 'We could not find a servant for you, so take the value of your servant today as a promissory note.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not take except his servant or the promissory note that he gave him the first time; no extra is added to it.'

key_terms.لَا يَزْدَادُ عَلَيْهِ شَيْئاً: No extra is added to it (no interest/increase)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on settling a debt with a servant or promissory note without adding interest?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), quoting Imam Ali (AS), establishes the principle of 'no increase on the principal' (la yazdadu 'alayhi shay') in deferred payment contracts, preventing hidden interest (riba) when substituting goods. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the exact value of the initial exchange, ensuring that the creditor cannot claim extra value merely due to the delay or substitution of the specific item (servant) for its monetary equivalent.
